input.summary:
Case A, $20 partial offer. q (buyer acceptance) and p (win rate) are your own assumptions, not statistics.

Cost (window period, from compare_acceptance):
- q 0.5: best plan is Refund A, Refund B, Fight C at 84.52. The offer plan (Offer $20 A, Refund B, Fight C) costs 127.74, so the offer loses.
- q 0.7: best plan is still Refund A, Refund B, Fight C at 84.52. The offer plan costs 92, so the offer loses.
- q 0.9: the offer plan wins at 56.27, and it is also the best plan.
- Break-even acceptance is 0.742. The offer only pays off if you think the buyer is more than 74.2% likely to accept $20. "Likely to accept" at 0.7 is just under that line.

Win rate: p is 0.4 in the rate plan. I did not vary p, so I can't say how the result changes with a different win rate.

Dispute-rate plan (q 0.7, p 0.4):
- Counted rate is 1.30%.
- Worst case is 1.82%.
- Plan rates are 1.47% and 1.75%.
- The plan total is 92 and the best total is 84.52, using Refund A, Refund B, Fight C.
- I have no tool result on whether High Volume applies, so I won't say whether it does.

Bottom line: at q 0.7 a full refund on A is cheaper than the $20 offer. The offer is better only if you are fairly sure the buyer accepts (q 0.9 or higher gives it the win). The comparison widget is on the dashboard.
